mainTopic: Blemished and unblemished animals for בדק הבית and the מזבח; רבא and אביי on double prohibitions; who can make a תמורה; selling a בכור.
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא on the פסוק 'נדבה תעשה אתו ולנדר לא ירצה'. It teaches that a blemished animal may go to בדק הבית, as a נדר or a נדבה, but never to the מזבח. The גמרא shows that רבי and the תנא קמא argue about consecrating such an animal for נסכים money. The word 'אותו' teaches that giving an unblemished animal to בדק הבית breaks an עשה. רבי יהודה adds that it also breaks a לאו, which he learns from the word 'לאמר'; בר קפרא and בי רבי then explain this by splitting the word to find a hidden 'לא'. Next, רבא and אביי argue whether offering a blemished animal's limbs breaks both 'do not burn all of it' and 'do not burn part of it'. A ברייתא listing five prohibitions refutes אביי, even after his two attempts to defend himself. A new משנה then teaches that a כהן can make a תמורה only on his own animals, not on a חטאת, אשם, or בכור he received, and רבי עקיבא proves this from a פסוק. The גמרא ends with רב נחמן's view that a כהן may sell an unblemished live בכור only nowadays, and it defends him against רבא's challenge.

steps.title: A blemished animal may be given to Temple maintenance
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'נדבה תעשה אתו' as permission to give a blemished animal to בדק הבית. It learns from 'ולנדר' that this works as a נדר too, not only as a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You may offer it as a gift' refers to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance. I would only know a gift; where do I learn a vow? The verse says 'and for a vow'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts explaining the פסוק about a blemished animal. It says the first half of the פסוק allows giving such an animal to בדק הבית, as either a נדבה or a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נדבה תעשה אתו' could look like they allow offering a blemished animal on the מזבח. The ברייתא says no: they refer to בדק הבית, where a blemish does not matter. The extra word 'ולנדר' widens this permission to a נדר as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A freewill gift: 'this animal' is given, so if it is lost you owe nothing more
A vow: 'I take upon myself' to give, so if the animal is lost you must replace it
Property given for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח
The פסוק teaches (introduces the proof word)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think נדבה and נדר here mean 'any gift' and 'any promise' loosely. A נדבה is 'this animal' (no replacement if it dies), and a נדר is 'I take upon myself' (must replace).

phrases.english: "You may make it a gift offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:23. The פסוק is about an animal with a limb that is too long or too short.

phrases.english: this refers to consecrations for Temple maintenance;
and I would only know about a gift;
from where do we know a vow?
The verse says: "and for a vow."

steps.triggerLanguage: נְדָבָה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ זֶה קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא on the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished animal may be consecrated for בדק הבית, as either a נדבה or a נדר.

steps.title: A blemished animal may not be given to the altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'ולנדר לא ירצה' as forbidding a blemished animal for the מזבח. It learns that this applies to a נדבה as well, not only to a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it even be for the altar? The verse says 'and for a vow it will not be accepted', which means altar offerings. I would only know a vow; where do I learn a gift? The verse says 'gift'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and blocks a wrong reading. A blemished animal cannot be given for קרבנות on the מזבח, whether as a נדר or as a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ירצה', meaning 'accepted', fits only a קרבן that is accepted on the מזבח. So the second half of the פסוק must be about קדשי מזבח. The word 'נדבה' is then read into this half too, so the ban covers both kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (sets up a wrong idea to reject it)
Animals consecrated to be offered on the מזבח
It will not be accepted (as a קרבן)

phrases.english: Might one think even consecrations for the altar are allowed?
The verse says: "and for a vow it will not be accepted";
this refers to consecrations for the altar.
And I would only know about a vow;
from where do we know a gift?
The verse says: "gift."
phrases.notes: Here the word 'gift' from the start of the פסוק is also read together with 'it will not be accepted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the permission given in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished animal may not be consecrated for the מזבח, as either a נדר or a נדבה.

steps.title: רבי: 'Not accepted' means the body itself being offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that 'לא ירצה' speaks about a case where the animal's own body would be offered as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: 'It will not be accepted' — the verse speaks about the animal's body itself being accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his own reading of 'לא ירצה'. The ban is about an animal whose body would actually go on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ties the ban closely to the body of the animal being offered. At first glance this sounds the same as the תנא קמא. The next steps show that this wording hints at a real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The acceptance of its body (the animal itself offered as a קרבן)

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
"It will not be accepted" —
the verse is speaking about the acceptance of its body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second view on the same words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban of 'לא ירצה' is about the animal's body itself being offered.

steps.title: Isn't רבי saying the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי adds, since the תנא קמא also said 'לא ירצה' refers to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's statement because it seems to say nothing new. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree a blemished animal cannot go on the מזבח. If so, why does רבי's statement appear as a separate view? There must be some difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: That is the same as the first Tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3 as repeating step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions limit the ban to the מזבח, so רבי's view seems to add nothing.

steps.title: They argue about consecrating it for libation money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the difference: the תנא קמא gives מלקות even for consecrating a blemished animal so its money buys נסכים. רבי gives מלקות only when the body itself would be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't they argue about this? The תנא קמא holds that even if he consecrated it for נסכים money, he is also flogged. רבי holds that only where its body is accepted is he flogged, but for נסכים money he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a real argument between the two views. The case is someone who consecrates a blemished animal to be sold, with the money used to buy נסכים for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, anything going toward the מזבח counts, even money for נסכים, so one gets מלקות. רבי's words 'הרצאת גופו' limit the ban to the animal's own body being offered. So money for נסכים does not bring מלקות according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested explanation)
Money to buy wine and flour offerings for the מזבח

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this:
that the first Tanna holds:
even if he consecrated it for the money of libations —
he is also flogged;
and Rabbi holds:
where its body is accepted — that is when he is flogged;
but for the money of libations — he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by naming the point of argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between the two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי and the תנא קמא seem to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ on consecrating a blemished animal for נסכים money: the תנא קמא gives מלקות, and רבי does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, according to the תנא קמא, consecrating a blemished animal for נסכים is treated like consecrating it for the מזבח itself.

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts this explanation as proof that, for the תנא קמא, consecrating for נסכים counts like consecrating for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion and accepts the explanation from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the only way to explain the argument is the נסכים case, the ברייתא supports the earlier suggestion on the דף. That suggestion was that consecrating a blemished animal for נסכים brings מלקות.
steps.whatToRemember: A blemished animal may go to בדק הבית but not to the מזבח. The תנא קמא includes money for נסכים in the ban, and רבי limits the ban to the animal's own body.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the תנא קמא, consecrating a blemished animal for נסכים money brings מלקות like consecrating it for the מזבח.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'אותו' in 'נדבה תעשה אותו' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need 'it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new detail of the same פסוק, the word 'אותו'. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'נדבה תעשה'. The extra word 'אותו', meaning 'it', must be there to limit or exclude something.

phrases.english: But why do I need the word "it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question on the פסוק from step 1.

steps.title: Only blemished animals go to Temple maintenance
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'אותו' that only a blemished animal may be given to בדק הבית. So one who gives an unblemished animal there transgresses an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught: 'You may make it a gift' — 'it' you may make a gift, but you may not make an unblemished animal a gift for Temple maintenance. From here they said: one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance transgresses a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'אותו' limits the permission to the blemished animal. An unblemished animal belongs on the מזבח, not in בדק הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותו' means 'this one', the blemished animal, and excludes an unblemished one. Since this exclusion comes from a positive phrase ('תעשה'), so far we only have an עשה. The next step adds a לאו as well.

keyTerms.meaning: An unblemished animal, fit for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אותו' teaches that only a blemished animal may go to בדק הבית. Giving an unblemished animal to בדק הבית transgresses an עשה.

phrases.english: For that which is taught:
"You may make it a gift offering" —
"it" you may make a gift,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה תָּמִים נְדָבָה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: but you may not make an unblemished animal a gift for Temple maintenance.
From here they said:
one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance —
transgresses a positive commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אותו' excludes an unblemished animal from being given to בדק הבית. Doing so transgresses an עשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule: unblemished animals are meant for the מזבח, and giving them to בדק הבית is forbidden by an עשה.

steps.title: The ברייתא adds a לאו from 'לאמר'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: giving an unblemished animal to בדק הבית also breaks a לאו. This is learned from the word 'לאמר' at the start of the פרשה, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know he also breaks a prohibition? Because the verse says 'And ה׳ spoke to משה, saying'. This teaches that the whole section counts as a prohibition. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It adds that a לאו is broken too, not just an עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed only an עשה, learned from 'אותו'. Now רבי יהודה says the opening word 'לאמר' turns every command in this פרשה into a לאו. So the person also breaks a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition; breaking one can bring מלקות

phrases.english: And from where do we know he also breaks a prohibition?
As it says: 'And ה׳ spoke to Moshe, saying'
This teaches that the whole section is a prohibition.
These are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding a לאו on top of the עשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every command in the פרשה of ויקרא כב counts as a לאו because of the word 'לאמר' (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: רבי asks how 'לאמר' shows a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks בר קפרא how the word 'לאמר' implies a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to בר קפרא: How do we see that from this word?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks a simple question: how does the plain word 'saying' show that something is forbidden? This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לאמר' normally just introduces speech. רבי wants to know where the hint of a prohibition is inside the word.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do we see this? How is it implied?

phrases.english: רבי said to בר קפרא:
How is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's derivation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word 'לאמר' hints at a לאו.

steps.title: בר קפרא: read it as 'לא' is said about these things
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא splits 'לאמר' into 'לא' plus 'נאמר': a 'no' is said about these matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it is written 'לאמר', read it as: 'לא' (no) is said about these matters.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא answers by splitting the word into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לאמר' is read as 'לא' plus 'נאמר'. That means the word 'no' is stated over this whole section, so its commands count as prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Saying', the word being split apart here
Matters, meaning the commands in the section

phrases.english: He said to him: Because it is written 'saying'
'No' is said about these matters.
phrases.notes: He is reading 'לאמר' as two words: 'לא' (no) and 'נאמר' (is said).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאמר' is read as 'לא נאמר': a 'no' is stated on these matters.

steps.title: The school of רבי reads it as 'do not say'
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי gives a second reading: 'לא אמור', meaning 'do not say'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the school of רבי they say: read it as 'לא אמור', do not say.
steps.whatsHappening: A second way to find the 'no' inside the word 'לאמר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'לאמר' becomes 'לא' plus 'אמור', 'do not say'. Either way the word holds a 'לא', so the section carries a prohibition. Only the split of the word is different.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not say', a second reading of לאמר

phrases.english: In the school of רבי they say:
'Do not say.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the same word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאמר' is read as 'לא אמור', a prohibition.
steps.whatToRemember: The לאו for giving an unblemished animal to בדק הבית comes from the word 'לאמר', split to show a hidden 'לא'.

steps.title: רבא: offering a blemished animal's limbs breaks two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: About offering the limbs of blemished animals on the מזבח, רבא says the person breaks both 'do not burn all of it' and 'do not burn part of it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If someone brings the limbs of blemished animals up on the מזבח, רבא says he breaks the prohibition of 'do not burn all of it' and also 'do not burn part of it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a disagreement between אמוראים. This step gives רבא's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier ברייתא listed both 'do not burn all of it' and 'do not burn part of it'. רבא treats them as two separate prohibitions, so one act breaks both and earns two sets of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a blemish, not fit to be offered
'Do not burn': the prohibition on burning on the מזבח

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who brings up the limbs of blemished animals
onto the מזבח,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תַּקְטִירוּ כּוּלּוֹ״
phrases.english: רבא says: he breaks 'do not burn all of it'
and 'do not burn part of it'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַמַּעֲלֶה אֵבְרֵי בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion, separate from the 'לאמר' derivation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering a blemished animal's limbs breaks two separate prohibitions.

steps.title: אביי: no double מלקות for a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees: we do not give מלקות for a לאו שבכללות, so there are no separate מלקות for each part.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: We do not give מלקות for a general prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the other side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All of it' and 'part of it' come from one verse. To אביי that makes it a single לאו covering several things, a לאו שבכללות. So the person does not get two sets of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A general prohibition: one לאו that covers several things

phrases.english: אביי says:
We do not give lashes for a general prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no separate מלקות for a לאו שבכללות.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי agrees the act is forbidden. He only disputes whether it earns two separate sets of מלקות.

steps.title: A ברייתא counts five separate prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: consecrating blemished animals for the מזבח breaks five separate categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who consecrates blemished animals for the מזבח breaks five separate prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source against אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list of five counts 'all of it' and 'part of it' separately. That fits רבא, who treats them as two prohibitions, and it goes against אביי.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who consecrates blemished animals for the מזבח
breaks five separate prohibitions,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that no separate מלקות are given here
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא counts 'all' and 'part' as two separate prohibitions, so they are not one general לאו.

steps.title: This seems to refute אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this ברייתא seems to refute אביי. אביי answers in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא seems to refute אביי. This sets up אביי's defense in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For now the ברייתא seems to knock down אביי's view and support רבא's view of two separate prohibitions. אביי answers this in the next step, and the back-and-forth continues until step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; that view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: Offering a blemished animal's limbs breaks both 'do not burn all of it' and 'do not burn part of it' (רבא). אביי's לאו שבכללות argument is challenged here. He defends it twice, and the refutation becomes final later in the amud.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of אביי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge against אביי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now the ברייתא seems to refute אביי; he answers it in the next step.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא is talking about different people
steps.stepSummary: אביי defends himself: the ברייתא of five לאוין describes different people, not one person breaking all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The ברייתא is teaching about different men.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the ברייתא that was used against him. He says it is not one person who breaks all five; one man burned the whole animal and another man burned only part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds there are no separate מלקות for 'burning all' and 'burning part' on one person. So he reads the list of five as covering several different people. Each person breaks only some of the לאוין, and nobody gets punished twice for one act.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is teaching about different men!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation from the ברייתא in steps 15–16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: several different people, not one person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say one person breaks all five לאוין, including both 'burning all' and 'burning part'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five are spread across different people, so no single person gets two punishments for the burning.

steps.title: The word 'violates' is singular
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer from the wording: the ברייתא says 'עובר' (he violates), in the singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about different men, why does it say 'violates' (singular)? It should have said 'they violate' (plural)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer using one word in the ברייתא. A singular verb points to one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא meant several people, it would use the plural form עוברין. It says עובר, so it is describing one man who breaks all five לאוין. That knocks out אביי's reading.

phrases.english: If it is about different men — 'violates'?!
It should have said 'they violate'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the ברייתא speaks about different people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The singular verb עובר shows the ברייתא means one person; for several people it would say עוברין.

steps.title: It must be one man, so אביי seems refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the ברייתא speaks of one man, which refutes אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it is about one man, and this is a refutation of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this round. Since the ברייתא means one person, אביי's view seems to be refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One man breaks all five לאוין, including both 'burning all' and 'burning part'. That means a person does get counted for both. This goes against אביי's rule that a לאו שבכללות brings no separate מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: a refutation; the view is knocked down

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious it is about one man,
and it is a refutation of Abaye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּחַד גַּבְרָא, וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the wording challenge in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is about one person, so it stands against אביי, at least until he tries another answer.

steps.title: אביי swaps one item in the list
steps.stepSummary: אביי tries a new answer: take 'burning part' out of the list of five and put 'collecting the blood' in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Take out 'burning part of it' and put in 'collecting the blood'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second defense. He changes which five לאוין the ברייתא is counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'burning part' is not one of the five, the ברייתא no longer counts burning twice. To keep the number at five, אביי adds 'collecting the blood' instead. Now the ברייתא fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: burning part of it on the מזבח
collecting the animal's blood in a vessel

phrases.english: Abaye said: Take out 'burning part of it',
and put in 'collecting the blood'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַפֵּיק הַקְטָרַת מִקְצָתוֹ, וְעַיֵּיל קַבָּלַת הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new defense after the first one failed in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the list of items being counted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The five לאוין include both 'burning all' and 'burning part'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five include 'collecting the blood' instead of 'burning part', so burning is counted only once.

steps.title: Only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: 'collecting the blood' is the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, not the תנא קמא, so אביי cannot put it in the first list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Collecting the blood — רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it counts, but the תנא קמא does not! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's swap. Only one opinion in the ברייתא counts collecting the blood, and it is not the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of five belongs to the תנא קמא, and he does not count blood collection as a לאו. So אביי cannot place it in the תנא קמא's list. The גמרא leaves this as a strong difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds it / he does not hold it
it is difficult; a question left unanswered

phrases.aramaic: קַבָּלַת דָּם — לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Collecting the blood — Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds it,
the first tanna does not hold it? It is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבָּלַת דָּם — לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִית לֵיהּ, לְתַנָּא קַמָּא לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's swap from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's move of putting 'collecting the blood' into the list of five
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list of five is the תנא קמא's, and only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts blood collection, so it cannot be part of that list.

steps.title: Another version: the first part is the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the attack: since the end of the ברייתא is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the beginning must be the רבנן, who do not count blood collection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: Since the end of the ברייתא is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the beginning must be the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same challenge to אביי. It is setting up the final ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה only in its last part, where blood collection is added. So the first part, the list of five, is the רבנן, and it cannot include blood collection. That takes away אביי's swap.

keyTerms.meaning: the last part of a teaching
the first part of a teaching

phrases.english: Another version: But since the last part
is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
the first part is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The 'Rabbis' here are the same as the תנא קמא, who do not count collecting the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: וְהָא מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the attack of step 21 in a second version.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's swap of 'burning part' for 'collecting the blood'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last part being רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה shows the first part is the רבנן, who do not count blood collection.

steps.title: אביי is fully refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the refutation of אביי stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of אביי is a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the whole discussion: אביי's view is knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of אביי's defenses failed. The ברייתא speaks of one person, and its list really includes both 'burning all' and 'burning part'. So רבא's view, that a person breaks both לאוין, stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Offering blemished animals on the מזבח breaks both 'do not burn all of it' and 'do not burn part of it'. אביי's argument that there are no separate מלקות here was fully refuted.

phrases.english: The refutation of Abaye is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 22 and the whole back-and-forth.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי is refuted; רבא's view of two separate לאוין stands.

steps.title: Each person can make a תמורה on his own animals
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: כהנים can make a תמורה on their own animals, and ישראלים on theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The כהנים make a תמורה on their own animals, and ישראלים make a תמורה on their own animals.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the basic rule that whoever owns the animal is the one who can make a תמורה on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה happens when someone tries to switch a קרבן for another animal; both end up holy. The משנה says this works for anyone on his own קרבן, כהן or ישראל. The key point is ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: they make a תמורה (try to swap a holy animal for another)

phrases.english: MISHNA: The priests substitute for their own,
and Israelites substitute for their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the debate about אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person, כהן or ישראל, can make a תמורה on a קרבן that belongs to him.

steps.title: כהנים cannot make a תמורה on these three
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three animals a כהן cannot make a תמורה on: a חטאת, an אשם, and a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים do not make a תמורה on a חטאת, an אשם, or a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three exceptions for כהנים. These animals reach the כהן from a ישראל, and they do not count as the כהן's own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the rule in step 24: you can only make a תמורה on your own animal. A חטאת or אשם that a כהן gets from a ישראל is not his. The משנה puts the בכור in the same group.

keyTerms.meaning: a firstborn animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: The priests do not substitute for a sin offering,
nor for a guilt offering, nor for a firstborn.
phrases.notes: He means ones a כהן receives from a ישראל, not the כהן's own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים מְמִירִין לֹא בְּחַטָּאת וְלֹא בְּאָשָׁם וְלֹא בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives exceptions to the general rule of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן cannot make a תמורה on a חטאת, אשם, or בכור he received.

steps.title: Why not on a בכור?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי asks why a כהן cannot make a תמורה on a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Why can they not make a תמורה on a בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי questions the third item on the list. He is setting up רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is handed over to the כהן as his own, so it seems to belong to him. If so, he should be able to make a תמורה on it, like any owner. רבי יוחנן בן נורי wants to know why the בכור is put with the חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:
For what reason do they not substitute for a firstborn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one item from the list in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a בכור, which seems to belong to the כהן, is treated like a חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the בכור is a gift like חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the בכור, like the חטאת and אשם, is a gift to the כהן, so the same rule applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: A חטאת and an אשם are a gift to the כהן, and a בכור is a gift to the כהן. Just as no תמורה is made on a חטאת and an אשם, so too no תמורה is made on a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers with a comparison. All three animals reach the כהן the same way, as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees a כהן cannot make a תמורה on a חטאת or אשם he received. רבי עקיבא says the בכור is the same kind of thing, a gift handed to the כהן. So it follows the same rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן can make a תמורה only on his own קרבן. A חטאת, אשם, or בכור he receives from a ישראל is a gift, and he cannot make a תמורה on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
A sin offering and a guilt offering are a gift to the priest,
and a firstborn is a gift to the priest.

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם אֵין מְמִירִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as for a sin offering and guilt offering one does not substitute,
so too for a firstborn one does not substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן בן נורי's question from step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור is a gift to the כהן, like the חטאת and אשם, so the same 'no תמורה' rule applies to it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי rejects the comparison to חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues that a בכור is different from a חטאת and אשם, because a כהן owns a בכור while it is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: How can you compare them? A כהן cannot make a תמורה with a חטאת or an אשם because he does not own them while they are alive. But a בכור he does own while it is alive, so why shouldn't he be able to make a תמורה with it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי pushes back on רבי עקיבא's answer from the previous step, saying the comparison does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חטאת and אשם, the כהן only gets a share of the meat after it is offered, so he never owns the live animal. A בכור is handed to the כהן alive and becomes his, so the reason for the חטאת and אשם should not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (a way of pointing out a difference between two cases)
Makes a תמורה, meaning he swaps a regular animal onto a holy one

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
How can you compare? If he cannot make a substitute
with a sin offering and a guilt offering,
which the priests do not acquire while they are alive,
phrases.notes: The כהנים only get to eat these after they are offered, so the live animal never becomes theirs.

phrases.english: will you say the same about a firstborn,
which they do acquire while it is alive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's comparison from step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's comparison of a בכור to a חטאת and אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason a כהן cannot make a תמורה on a חטאת and אשם is that he does not own them alive. A בכור he does own alive, so the reason does not carry over.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא proves from a פסוק that only the original owner can make a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that a תמורה takes effect where the animal first became holy, which is in the owner's house, not with the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: But the תורה already said, 'It and its substitute shall be holy.' Where did the animal become holy? In the owner's house. So the תמורה too can only happen in the owner's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a new answer, based on a פסוק, that does not depend on whether the כהן owns the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the animal and its תמורה together, so the תמורה belongs with whoever held the animal when it became holy. A בכור becomes holy at birth in the owner's house, before the כהן gets it, so the כהן, who received it later, cannot make a תמורה on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its substitute, the animal swapped onto it
The owner's house, meaning while it is with the original owner

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה can only be made by the owner who held the animal when it first became holy. That is why a כהן cannot make a תמורה on a בכור he received.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the rule away from 'who owns the animal now' and onto 'where did the holiness first take effect.' That closes the משנה's list of animals a כהן cannot make a תמורה on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
But hasn't it already been stated:
"Then it and its substitute shall be holy,"
Where does holiness take effect on it?
In the owner's house,
phrases.notes: A בכור becomes holy the moment it is born, while it is still with the owner and before the כהן gets it.

phrases.english: so too the substitute happens in the owner's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן בן נורי's challenge with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source that switches to a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the כהן owns the live בכור, he should be able to make a תמורה on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תמורה follows where the holiness first took effect, in the owner's house, so the כהן cannot make one on a בכור.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: a בכור may be sold and used for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה saying a בכור can be sold (unblemished only alive, blemished alive or slaughtered) and used to marry a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: A בכור may be sold while alive if it has no blemish, and alive or slaughtered if it has a blemish. A כהן may also use it to marry a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה about a כהן's ownership of a בכור. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the בכור as the כהן's real property, since he can sell it and marry with it. The open question is when this applies, which רב נחמן will address next.

phrases.english: Gemara
We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת מעשר שני.

phrases.english: A firstborn, one may sell it
if unblemished, while alive,
and if blemished, alive or slaughtered,
and one may betroth a woman with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a new source about the כהן's ownership of a בכור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may sell a בכור (unblemished only alive) and use it for קידושין.

steps.title: רב נחמן limits the משנה to nowadays
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the משנה's rule about selling an unblemished בכור applies only when there is no בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This was taught only for nowadays, since the כהן owns it. But when the בית המקדש stands, an unblemished בכור is set aside to be offered, so it may not be sold alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains when the משנה's rule applies, limiting it to the time after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nowadays an unblemished בכור cannot be offered, so it really belongs to the כהן and he may sell it. When the בית המקדש stands, it is meant for the מזבח, so the כהן's ownership is not strong enough to sell it.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
It stands ready to be offered

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
They taught this only for the present time,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאִית לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּויהּ
phrases.english: since the priest has ownership rights in it
(since the priest has a share in it),
phrases.notes: These words in round brackets are in the regular printed גמרא, but the corrected text leaves them out.

phrases.english: but when the Temple is standing,
since an unblemished one stands ready to be offered,
one may not sell it unblemished while alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה from step 30 to nowadays
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unblemished live בכור may be sold only nowadays, not when the בית המקדש stands.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the word 'alive'
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that 'alive, not slaughtered' only makes sense when the בית המקדש stands, so the משנה must allow selling then too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: The משנה says it may be sold unblemished while alive, so alive yes, slaughtered no. When is that? If nowadays, is there ever a slaughtered unblemished בכור? So it must be when the בית המקדש stands, and still the משנה says it may be sold alive. That shows the כהן owns it then too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן by reading an inference out of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'alive' suggests the משנה is contrasting it with a slaughtered unblemished בכור. That case only exists when the בית המקדש stands, because nowadays an unblemished בכור is not slaughtered. So the משנה must be talking about the time of the בית המקדש, which goes against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
One may sell it unblemished while alive,
alive, yes; slaughtered, no.
When is this?
If you say in the present time,
is there such a thing as a slaughtered unblemished one?
phrases.notes: Nowadays an unblemished בכור is never slaughtered, because no offerings are brought.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it means
when the Temple is standing,
and it still teaches:
one may sell it unblemished while alive,
(this shows the priest has ownership rights in it)!
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets and some leave them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's limitation in step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the משנה applies only nowadays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Alive' implies 'not slaughtered,' and a slaughtered unblemished בכור exists only when the בית המקדש stands, so the משנה allows selling even then.

steps.title: The word 'alive' is not meant to exclude anything
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה really means nowadays, and 'alive' is not contrasting with 'slaughtered.' It simply teaches that even nowadays one may sell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה really is talking about nowadays. Does it actually say 'alive yes, slaughtered no'? It came to teach just this: that even nowadays one may sell an unblemished בכור alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge by rejecting his inference from the word 'alive.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read 'alive' as excluding 'slaughtered.' The answer is that the משנה never said that. The phrase simply states the rule, that selling is allowed nowadays, so רב נחמן's limitation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (used to keep an original position)
It came to teach us that very point

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a כהן may sell an unblemished live בכור only nowadays. The word 'alive' in the משנה describes the case and does not exclude a slaughtered animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume every word in a משנה is there to exclude the opposite case. Here the גמרא says 'alive' just describes the case.

phrases.english: No, actually it is the present time.
Does it teach:
'one may sell it unblemished while alive, yes,'
'slaughtered, no'?
It came to teach us that point itself,
that in the present time too
one may sell it unblemished while alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference drawn from the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Alive' implies 'not slaughtered,' so the משנה must be about the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Alive' excludes nothing. The משנה teaches that even nowadays an unblemished בכור may be sold alive.
